problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions of the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ for $0\le x<2\pi ,$  what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}?$

feedback.problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions of the equation $2\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\sqrt{2}=0$ for $0\le x<2\pi ,$  what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, isolating $\operatorname{sin}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\sqrt{2} & =0 \\ 2\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =\sqrt{2} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡x & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})=\frac{\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\frac{\pi }{4}$ lies inside the required domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=\frac{\pi }{4}.$

Our first solution lies in the first quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{4}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the second quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{4}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13951962/assets/269d503189ab1027c3d8028542ef0c6a0e2f146aef0f7916691428866ce1b894.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $2$nd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi -\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions are $x=\frac{\pi }{4},\frac{3\pi }{4}.$

Finally, 

$$
{x}_{1}{x}_{2}=\frac{\pi }{4}\cdot \frac{3\pi }{4}=\frac{3{\pi }^{2}}{16}.
$$
